subject: Intermittent packet failures after private backhaul cutover - SNAT/SG surface
messages:
From: Aaron Shaw <aaron.shaw@brightline.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, netops@brightline.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent failures after private backhaul cutover

Hi Karthik / Redwood team,

We cut the private backhaul (Brightline -> Redwood VPC) Tuesday night as planned. Since the cutover we've been seeing intermittent failures for a subset of sessions that traverse the new transit path. Impact: ~1.5% of API calls from our East region result in TCP RSTs or very short connections (requests that fail within 200-600ms).

Attached is a short pcap and a traceroute. Our onprem firewall is showing a small number of translated ports in the SNAT pool that correspond to the failures. We haven't changed application code. Symptoms look like either: 1) SNAT port reuse/exhaustion with subsequent RSTs, 2) security-group / firewall dropping ephemeral port ranges post-translation, or 3) MTU/fragmentation causing session failures for specific flow sizes.

Can Redwood ops take a look and advise next steps? This is affecting a handful of production customers (we're throttling requests to mitigate), but would like a short-term fix followed by a permanent configuration change.

I've attached brightline_pcap_extract_0310.pcap and a short syslog excerpt.

Thanks,
Aaron Shaw
Network Operations | Brightline Health
aaron.shaw@brightline.com
netops@brightline.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Aaron Shaw <aaron.shaw@brightline.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures after private backhaul cutover

Aaron — thanks for the heads up and the pcap. I'm escalating this to our connectivity and field-eng teams. Quick initial asks so we can triage in parallel: 

- Can you confirm the timing window (UTC) when the failures are most frequent?
- Please paste the BGP adjacency state (show ip bgp summary or equivalent) and the onprem SNAT pool utilization snapshot.
- Any recent security-group changes on your side?

Hypothesis/routing checklist we'll run immediately:
1) Verify SNAT port pool capacity and conntrack timeouts (server and on-Redwood edge).
2) Inspect SG/firewall for deny rules targeting ephemeral port ranges (e.g. 32768-61000) after SNAT.
3) MTU path-check between Brightline edge and the Redwood edge, including DF-set flows.
4) Check for asymmetric routing / traffic steering differences that could cause RSTs on return path.

Marissa / Mina — can you pull the pcap and trace now and do a quick correlation with our edge conntrack/translation logs? If we can replicate in staging, we'll test a temporary SG rule to allow the ephemeral range and a short SNAT pool expansion.

I'll schedule a short War Room if we need live coordination.

- Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering (acting on connectivity)
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Aaron Shaw <aaron.shaw@brightline.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures after private backhaul cutover

Quick triage notes — I imported the pcap and here's what I see:

- Multiple TCP flows from Brightline clients show SYN -> SYN/ACK -> immediate RST from our edge (timestamps within 300-450ms of SYN).
- The post-NAT source port on several flows maps to the same SNAT translation sockets repeatedly before they fail; suggests port reuse or conntrack exhaustion.
- I also see ICMP "fragmentation needed" for one flow with MSS ~1460 when packet size >1400.

I've attached a short config diff (config_diff_before_after_0311.txt) capturing recent ACL/SecurityGroup rules we applied during the cutover window; nothing obvious denies ephemeral ports but the NAT pool size looks smaller in the new path.

Immediate mitigations to test (low-risk):
1) Temporarily expand SNAT port pool on Redwood edge by +20% and increase conntrack entries for the flow table.
2) Add a short-lived SG allow rule for ephemeral ports 32768-61000 between Brightline CIDR and Redwood private subnets for 2 hours.
3) Run a directed MTU probe and enable MSS clamp to 1400 on the transit tunnel if we continue to see "fragmentation needed".

If Aaron can approve a 20-minute change window, we'll make the SNAT expansion and the SG rule and monitor. If the flows stabilize, we'll roll in a permanent config and update runbooks.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: config_diff_before_after_0311.txt
From: Aaron Shaw <aaron.shaw@brightline.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures after private backhaul cutover

Thanks Marissa — we pulled SNAT usage graphs and the busiest window is 2027-03-10 08:45-09:30 UTC. Our appliance shows the NAT pool utilization hitting 94% at peaks; we do see port churn matching the timestamps in your pcap. We're comfortable with a short window — please proceed with your mitigations.

One ask: can you also capture conntrack stats on Redwood edge (active entries, timeouts) before/after the change and share? We'll compare with our appliance counters.

-Aaron
Aaron Shaw
Network Operations | Brightline Health
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Aaron Shaw <aaron.shaw@brightline.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures after private backhaul cutover

Aaron — approved. Proposed change window: 2027-03-11 10:00–10:20 UTC (20 min). Plan:

1) Snapshot conntrack/stats and export to Drive (pre-change).
2) Expand SNAT port pool by +25% on the edge for Brightline CIDR; increase conntrack max entries by 30%.
3) Add temporary SG allow rule for ephemeral range (32768-61000) scoped between Brightline <-> Redwood private subnets for 30 minutes.
4) Active testing by Brightline to reproduce traffic while we monitor.
5) If errors drop below 0.3% for 15 mins, keep change and create a permanent runbook. If not, roll back immediately and open deeper debug.

I'll post the Drive link and capture logs (conntrack dump, SNAT table) as we go. Laura — please coordinate the rollout and be ready to escalate to infra if the edge kernel shows pressure.

- Karthik
From: Aaron Shaw <aaron.shaw@brightline.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failures after private backhaul cutover (Resolved)

Team — quick post-mortem: we ran the SNAT pool + SG change during the 11 Mar window. After the changes the RST rate dropped to ~0.1% within 10 minutes and has stayed low. The conntrack table on Redwood edge showed reduced churn after the pool increase; we've attached a short post-change sample in the shared Drive.

Root cause (most likely): the new backhaul path used a smaller SNAT pool configuration combined with stricter SG rules on the translated source ports. When the pool hit high utilization, port reuse and conntrack churn caused intermittent session resets for a subset of flows. MTU/fragmentation was secondary for a very small set of large-payload flows and was remediated by enabling MSS clamp on the transit tunnel.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — appreciate the coordination (Marissa, Mina, Laura, Karthik). Please update the runbook and we'll schedule a follow-up to formalize permanent config changes.

Best,
Aaron Shaw
Network Operations | Brightline Health
